MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JANUARY 8, 2024

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR YOO at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Nicklas, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar, Romanelli

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, DECEMBER 4, 2023

COMMISSIONER OLSON, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, DECEMBER 4, 2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

B.  2023 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JULY 1, 2023 THROUGH JANUARY
  4, 2024.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 6B.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

Items taken out of order.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230533; LOCATION: 2533 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH; APPLICANT: DOMINGO OTTOLIA; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-230534) for the 1,387 square foot two-story addition to an existing two-
  story single-family residence, and a Variance (V-230551) to exceed the height-to-setback
  ratio in the west side yard. The proposal includes an interior remodel of 665 square feet
  of the existing residence, a new 630 square foot rear balcony on the upper floor, a new
  395 square foot rear covered patio on the lower floor, and minor improvements to the front

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 8, 2024
  1
   façade and yard.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. The home will
maintain a farmhouse style. The existing home is 1,879 SF and the proposed home is 2,932 SF,
which is within the median home size in the neighborhood. The existing home sits in a sloped
area and is minimally visible from the street. A Variance is requested to continue to exceed the
height to setback ratio in the west side. Staff can support the Variance findings based on the
property’s single-family residential use, the existing non-conformity of the site, and the
development patterns of the area. The proposed project is consistent with Land Use Goal 2.7 of
the Ccity’s General Plan.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt
Resolution No. PA-230533, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if there were any comments from the neighbors. Assistant
Planner Kawagoe stated that she believes that the neighbors were contacted about the upper
deck and there were no comments received by staff.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

AYES: Yoo, Nicklas, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar, Romanelli
ABSTAIN:

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked for the location of the trash yard area to be added to the plans.
Domingo Ottolia, Project Architect, stated that this will be shown on plans and that they will be
located on the west side of the property adjacent to the garage.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if parking for construction vehicles has been addressed. Mr.
Ottolia stated that this has not been discussed but can be added to the conditions of approval and
they will address this prior to construction.

Jennifer Taggart, Property Owner, stated that this is a horse property and there is a designated
area in the rear of the property for horse manure and the trash associated with it. She also stated
that she and the neighbor discussed the project; she agreed that after construction, if necessary,
there will be vegetation placed on the upper deck for any privacy issues. Ms. Taggart stated that
there is sufficient parking for construction vehicles on the site, and that they were not planning to
park on the street.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230533.

AYES: Yoo, Nicklas, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar, Romanelli
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-
230533, inclusive of a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-230534) and Variance (V-
230551). There is a 20-day appeal period, whereby any member of the public or the City Council
by its own motion may appeal this project.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT

Director Naughton provided a presentation with the objective to get direction on the desired urban

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 8, 2024
  2
 form.

In terms of Street Frontage and Ground-Floor Setbacks, the following questions were posed to
the commission:

  •  Minimum or Zero Setbacks
  o Would it be appropriate to establish maximum street setbacks?
  o In the case of larger street setbacks for outdoor dining or similar use, what would
  be the maximum allowable street setback?
  o Do we want to prescribe corner setbacks to accommodate public or semi-public
  use?

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN used the example of Merrill Gardens where part of the
building is setback and the entrance is disconnected from the community. She asked if there are
circumstances where buildings should be setback or if they should always be fronted along the
street.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that
parking will need to be in the rear or structured parking if buildings are pulled up to the street, and
parking requirements will need to be modified in the future.

CHAIR YOO asked about the variable setback approach. Director Naughton stated that a
“scorecard” could be developed tied to the use. Currently, the code does not require ground floor
retail. The question was posed whether the ground floor should be required to be non-residential.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that the scorecard may be a better way to
incentivize developers to design projects with non-residential on the ground floor.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if a Variance would be required for more than the
maximum allowable setback. Director Naughton stated that staff would need to make the findings
in order to support it.

Director Naughton stated that staff can bring back options for what the scorecards could look at,
based on the uses.

Director Naughton asked if there should be additional corner setbacks. COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN stated that this should be required and there was consensus among the
commissioners.

  •  Massing
  o Should the maximum height be increased to accommodate ground-floor
  commercial plate height 12’-20’?
  o Should a maximum number of stories be established, or should it rely on building
  height alone?

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation with visuals including various variables for
redevelopment of the five opportunity sites.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that the first floor should be required to be a certain
height, for example 16’. She also stated that she has no issue with the building being a straight
build up with no step-backs as long as there are elements such as balconies or a courtyard area
to prevent it from looking like a linear line.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that he does not believe that excessively high buildings are
necessary. He stated that having a 50’ maximum could provide for four stories with a large plate
on the first floor. He asked if four stories will be economically feasible for the cost of the land.
Director Naughton stated in the Land Use Element market study that for a project to have a
positive residual value, it would need to be closer to 90-units to the acre with affordable housing.
Currently, developers can use the City’s and the State’s Density program in order to get
concessions to the development standards, which could be the height.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN suggested having a point-system to get a higher elevation
but stay within four floors.

  •  Smaller Block Patterns
  o How could the code incentivize the creation of smaller block patterns?

Director Naughton stated that the Land Use Element talks about smaller block patterns to create
pedestrian connectivity. This could also be included in the scorecard.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JANUARY 8, 2024
  3
   •  Flexible Ground Floor Space

Director Naughton stated that per the discussion, this could also be included in the scorecard.

Director Naughton stated that there are a variety of styles in the commercial district. The Land
Use Element talks about using local materials. When this was discussed previously, the direction
from the Planning Commission was to keep it flexible.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS stated that there should be broad parameters to some commonality.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN expressed her concern with developers who may produce
very modern designs that do not fit in with the community.

COMMISSIONER OLSON suggested design guidelines for certain areas to be compatible with
what may already exist.

Director Naughton stated that staff can look into zones, although it may be difficult to find one
cohesive style in any one stretch.

Director Naughton stated that staff will discuss this with the City’s consultants and will return to
the commission with a scorecard with general architectural guidelines.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about the parking structure at the Promenade. Director
Naughton stated that the City is involved and has inspected the parking structure.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton asked the Planning Commission about moving meetings to Tuesday nights
to be in line with City Council meetings. The Planning Commission had no issue with moving the
meeting to Tuesday night.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

NONE

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR YOO adjourned the meeting at 8:35 p.m.

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on February 5, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.in the City
Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Victor Yoo, Chair

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
